$comment: Advisories knowingly accepted in the PRODUCTION dependency tree, read by scripts/audit-check.mjs.
Ships empty on purpose: an entry here is a vulnerability we are shipping. Add one only when there
is no fixed version and no way to drop the dependency.
Fields:
advisory      REQUIRED. The GHSA id from the advisory URL npm prints (GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx, from
https://github.com/advisories/...), or the npm-advisory-<number> fallback the
script prints for an advisory that has no GitHub advisory URL.
justification REQUIRED. Why it is acceptable to ship, in a sentence the next person can act on.
expires       REQUIRED. YYYY-MM-DD, the LAST day the suppression applies. After it, the finding
blocks again and the entry must be fixed or renewed.
package       OPTIONAL, and documentation only - see the matching rule below.
Rules the script enforces:
- Only those four field names. An unrecognised key (`expiry`, `packages`) is an error, because
an entry with a field the script ignores does not do what its diff looks like it does.
- expires at most 180 days out. An exception nobody has to re-argue is a policy change.
- One entry per advisory. Renew by editing the date, so the diff shows what actually changed.
- Anything malformed disables the WHOLE file - nothing is suppressed - so keep it valid JSON.
Matching is by advisory id alone. `package` is never part of it, because a package name is what
moves when a transitive dependency is re-parented, and a suppression that silently lapses on an
unrelated tree change is worse than none. The cost is real and worth knowing before you write an
entry: if this advisory later also lands on a SECOND package, this entry suppresses it there too,
carrying a justification written about the first. There is no way to scope an entry more narrowly -
so a justification that only holds for one package should say so, and be revisited if the advisory
spreads.
A finding printed as npm-advisory-unnamed-<n> cannot be listed here at all: that id is a position
in npm's report rather than an identity, so an entry holding one would drift onto a different
advisory.

$example.justification: No fixed release upstream; the parser is only reached by prisma's CLI, which does not run in production.
$example.expires: YYYY-MM-DD (at most 180 days out; a real date here would be a date somebody copied rather than chose)
